unlisted_practices: Establish a European-level training curriculum to build the literacy, capacity, and confidence of patient representatives to engage in AI design and governance.
Develop a toolbox that operationalises ethical and regulatory guidelines across the AI development process.
Create a compliance support tool integrating an interactive legal and ethical database with access to human legal expertise.
Embed data literacy in healthcare education.
Create structural incentives, such as linking funding eligibility to data literacy, to promote inclusive practices.
Strengthen public and academic sector leadership in AI development to reduce reliance on industry-led development.
Establish a multi-stakeholder advisory panel to engage throughout the development of regulatory frameworks for inclusive AI.
Make data collection an explicit, transparent, mutual process between data collectors and data subjects, particularly for vulnerable populations.
Organise bi-directional events so patients and developers gain mutual understanding.
Collect and disseminate grassroots success stories to inform policymakers and foster mutual learning.
Design AI systems to be inclusive from the start rather than retrospectively.
Embed mechanisms for local adaptation and value-sensitive design so standardised, interoperable AI systems remain responsive to context-specific needs.

screen.reason: This paper presents PREFER-IT, a transdisciplinary co-created framework/guideline for realizing inclusive medical AI developed via expert workshops rather than an empirical evaluation of an AI tool.
